question: Is the repo "meridian/web-app" release-ready?

invariants.assert: A named subject mention that misses its intended target never silently widens to org-wide/broader scope; widening is only ever a disclosed, terminal answered_with_gaps/needs_clarification outcome.
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker scope_resolution_outcome_in against this case's own resolution-profile expected_scope_resolution_outcome (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518) -- no longer a narrower no_internal_error placeholder.

invariants.assert: The run's derived wave4_case_result.v1 resolution_path equals this case's resolution-profiles/deterministic-v1.json entry's own resolution_path (null is a valid, asserted value for n/a-subject cases that never attempt mention resolution).

notes: Outcome judgment call, documented rather than guessed silently: world.json's generation profile (days_of_history=10, with_work_graph=true) gives meridian/web-app a live mix of open and closed work items -- no fixture pins a deterministic 'fully complete, zero remaining work' state for this repo (unlike sources.json's probe/source-current, which is a source-freshness fixture, not a completion fixture). status.single-project.remaining-work (same subject) legitimately expects to enumerate outstanding work, which would contradict a clean 'release-ready: yes' answer here -- so answered_with_gaps (readiness reported with caveats/open items flagged) is the more honest expectation than a bare answered. Documented as the deliberate call per this lane's brief rather than picked implicitly. [CORRECTED during Lane 2b codex round-1 remediation, 2026-08-06, from 'Is meridian/web-app release-ready?': question_interpreter.py's own module docstring states plainly 'a lowercase slug ... produces no mention' -- extract_mentions requires either a capitalized _NAME token or a QUOTED span adjacent to a closed kind noun (test_question_interpreter.py's proven pattern: 'How is repo "dev-health-ops" doing?'). The original bare, unquoted lowercase slug would extract ZERO typed mentions and silently degrade to org-wide/no-subject behavior -- exactly the false-pass risk codex's wrong-kind-collision finding named, generalized here to every other case that had the same bug.]
